scene.note: You read what the compiler says about Kasimir's lines and fix each mistake, until his bench sheet builds and prints.

steps.note: Kasimir's line adds the springs in stock to the springs just delivered.
The compiler stops and names the line where it expected something more.
With the statement finished, the bench sheet prints the springs on the shelf.
Kasimir works out the hands for today's clocks and prints them.
The compiler meets a name nobody made, and says which one.
The name in the print and the name of the variable have to match, letter for letter.
The bench sheet prints the hands Kasimir worked out.
Kasimir puts the width of the glass crystal into a variable to print it.
The compiler names two types: the value does not fit the box it goes into.
In a box of the right type, the width prints with its decimals.
Kasimir prints the oil one service takes, with two decimals.
The compiler does not know one name on the line, because the file never brought it in.
The line itself stays as Kasimir wrote it.
The bench sheet prints the oil with two decimals.
